q: Which of the following Indus Valley sites is famous for its ancient dockyard?
exp: Lothal (located in Gujarat near the Bhogava river) had a massive brick-lined dockyard used for maritime trade.

q: The 'Great Bath' of the Indus Valley Civilization was discovered at:
exp: The Great Bath, a large public water tank likely used for ritual bathing, was excavated at Mohenjodaro.

q: The famous 'Gayatri Mantra' is found in which Mandala of the Rig Veda?
exp: The Gayatri Mantra, dedicated to Savitri, is composed by Vishwamitra and appears in the 3rd Mandala of the Rig Veda.

q: Where did Gautama Buddha deliver his first sermon (Dharmachakrapravartana)?
exp: Buddha delivered his first sermon to five ascetics at the Deer Park (Isipatana) in Sarnath, near Varanasi.

q: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir under the patronage of which ruler?
exp: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held at Kundalvana in Kashmir under Kushan emperor Kanishka, presided over by Vasumitra.

q: Who deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts of Ashokan inscriptions in 1837?
exp: James Prinsep, an officer of the East India Company mint, deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in 1837.

q: Which Ashokan Rock Edict describes the horrors of the Kalinga War and Ashoka's remorse?
exp: Major Rock Edict XIII records Ashoka's victory over Kalinga and his subsequent turn towards Dhamma.

q: Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador who wrote 'Indica', visited the court of:
exp: Megasthenes was sent by Seleucus I Nicator as an ambassador to the Mauryan court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra.

q: The 'Prayag Prashasti' (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) celebrating Samudragupta's conquests was composed by:
exp: Harishena, the court poet and minister of Samudragupta, composed the Prayag Prashasti in classical Sanskrit.

q: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa-Hien (Faxian) visited India during the reign of:
exp: Fa-Hien visited India between 399 and 414 CE during the reign of Gupta emperor Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

q: The Aihole Inscription, which records the defeat of Harshavardhana by Pulakeshin II, was composed by:
exp: Ravikirti, the Jain court poet of Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, composed the Aihole Prashasti.

q: The famous Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur was built by which Chola ruler?
exp: Rajaraja Chola I completed the Brihadeeswarar Temple (Rajarajeshwaram) in 1010 CE; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: The Chola local self-government (village assemblies like Sabha and Ur) is famously detailed in the inscriptions of:
exp: The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I provide detailed rules for the election and functioning of village committees (Variyams).

q: Who among the following Delhi Sultans introduced the market control policy and the 'Dagh' (branding of horses) system?
exp: Alauddin Khalji introduced strict market price regulations, Dagh (horse branding), and Chehra (descriptive roll of soldiers).

q: The 'Iqta' system of land revenue assignment was institutionalized in the Delhi Sultanate by:
exp: Shams-ud-din Iltutmish institutionalized the Iqta system, dividing the empire into tracts assigned to officers (Iqtadars) in lieu of salary.

q: The Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of which Delhi Sultan?
exp: Ibn Battuta arrived in India in 1333 CE during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign and was appointed Qazi of Delhi.

q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 CE on the banks of the Tungabhadra river by:
opts: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I
exp: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama dynasty founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE.

q: Who authored the famous Telugu work 'Amuktamalyada'?
exp: Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva dynasty) authored Amuktamalyada in Telugu and Jambavati Kalyanam in Sanskrit.

q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526), which established Mughal rule in India, was fought between Babur and:
exp: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in April 1526 using artillery and the Tulughma tactic.

q: The 'Dahsala' (Zabti) land revenue system under Emperor Akbar was formulated by:
exp: Raja Todar Mal introduced the Ain-i-Dahsala system in 1580, fixing revenue based on the average produce and prices of the preceding ten years.

q: In the Mughal Mansabdari system, what did the terms 'Zat' and 'Sawar' denote respectively?
opts: Personal rank/salary and number of cavalrymen to maintain
exp: 'Zat' fixed the personal status and salary of a Mansabdar, while 'Sawar' indicated the number of cavalrymen he was required to maintain.

q: Who among the following Bhakti saints was a disciple of Ramananda and composed verses included in the Guru Granth Sahib?
exp: Kabir, a Nirguna Bhakti saint and disciple of Ramananda, criticized ritualism; many of his verses are preserved in the Guru Granth Sahib.

q: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was signed between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and:
exp: The Treaty of Purandar was signed on 11 June 1665 between Shivaji and Mughal commander Mirza Raja Jai Singh I.

q: In the Battle of Plassey (1757), the British East India Company forces were led by:
exp: Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal at Plassey on 23 June 1757, aided by Mir Jafar's defection.

q: The Battle of Buxar (1764) led to the signing of which treaty that granted the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the East India Company?
exp: The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) signed between Robert Clive and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II granted Diwani rights to the Company.

q: Which Act created the office of the Governor-General of Bengal and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta?
exp: The Regulating Act of 1773 made Warren Hastings the first Governor-General of Bengal and set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta in 1774.

q: Which Charter Act ended the commercial monopoly of the East India Company in India (except trade in tea and trade with China)?
exp: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly in India except for tea and trade with China, and allocated Rs 1 lakh for education.

q: The 'Ryotwari System' of land revenue settlement in the Madras Presidency was primarily developed by:
exp: Alexander Read and Thomas Munro introduced the Ryotwari system, where revenue was collected directly from the cultivators (ryots).

q: Sati was legally abolished in Bengal in 1829 during the tenure of which Governor-General?
exp: Lord William Bentinck passed Regulation XVII in December 1829 declaring Sati illegal, largely due to Raja Ram Mohan Roy's campaign.

q: Which princely state was the FIRST to be annexed by Lord Dalhousie under the 'Doctrine of Lapse'?
exp: Satara (1848) was the first state annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse, followed by Jaitpur & Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), and Nagpur (1854).

q: The 'Wood's Despatch' of 1854 is associated with reforms in which field?
exp: Wood's Despatch (1854), called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India', recommended universities in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.

q: Who led the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar (Jagdishpur)?
exp: Babu Kunwar Singh, the 80-year-old zamindar of Jagdishpur, led the 1857 uprising in Bihar with remarkable military skill.

q: The 'Ilbert Bill Controversy' (1883) occurred during the viceroyalty of:
exp: Lord Ripon's Ilbert Bill sought to allow senior Indian magistrates to try European British subjects, triggering fierce opposition from Europeans.

q: Who founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' (Truth-Seekers' Society) in 1873 in Maharashtra?
exp: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to fight caste oppression and promote education among marginalized communities and women.

q: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in December 1885?
exp: Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee presided over the first INC session at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, attended by 72 delegates.

q: The 'Drain of Wealth' theory was systematically put forward by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book:
opts: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
exp: Dadabhai Naoroji exposed British economic exploitation in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901).

q: The famous 'Surat Split' between the Moderates and Extremists in the Indian National Congress took place in:
exp: The INC split at the 1907 Surat Session (presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh) over the scope of the Swadeshi movement and presidency.

q: Which Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims for the first time in British India?
exp: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced communal representation via separate electorates for Muslims.

q: The 'Ghadar Party' was founded in 1913 in San Francisco primarily by:
opts: Lala Hardayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
Madam Bhikaji Cama and Shyamji Krishna Varma
Subhas Chandra Bose and Rash Behari Bose
exp: Sohan Singh Bhakna (President) and Lala Hardayal (Secretary) founded the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association, popularly known as the Ghadar Party.

q: The 'Lucknow Pact' of 1916 was an agreement signed between:
opts: British Government and Indian National Congress
Indian National Congress and All-India Muslim League
exp: The 1916 Lucknow Session saw both the reunion of Moderates & Extremists and the Lucknow Pact between the INC and the Muslim League.

q: Mahatma Gandhi's first Civil Disobedience movement in India was the:
exp: In 1917, Gandhi launched the Champaran Satyagraha in Bihar against the oppressive Tinkathia indigo plantation system.

q: The 'Dyarchy' system in the provinces was introduced by which Act?
exp: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced Dyarchy in provinces (dividing subjects into Reserved and Transferred); the 1935 Act abolished it in provinces.

q: Which incident led Mahatma Gandhi to abruptly call off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?
exp: After a violent clash at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP) where a police station was set ablaze, Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.

q: The 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was adopted by the Indian National Congress at its 1929 session in:
exp: At the 1929 Lahore Session presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the INC declared Purna Swaraj as its goal and fixed 26 January 1930 as Independence Day.

q: The 'Poona Pact' of 1932 was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar regarding:
opts: Separate electorates vs. reserved seats for Depressed Classes
exp: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates for Depressed Classes (proposed in the Communal Award) with increased reserved seats within the general electorate.

q: Who founded the 'Forward Bloc' in 1939 after resigning from the presidency of the Indian National Congress?
exp: Subhas Chandra Bose resigned after the Tripuri Session (1939) and formed the All India Forward Bloc within the Congress.

q: Who was chosen by Mahatma Gandhi as the FIRST Satyagrahi in the Individual Satyagraha of 1940?
exp: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first Individual Satyagrahi, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru as the second.

q: Mahatma Gandhi described which British proposal of 1942 as a 'post-dated cheque drawn on a crashing bank'?
exp: The Cripps Mission (March 1942) offered Dominion Status after World War II, which Gandhi famously dismissed as a post-dated cheque.

q: The 'Cabinet Mission' of 1946 was sent to India by British Prime Minister Clement Attlee. Who among the following was NOT a member of it?
exp: The three members of the Cabinet Mission (1946) were Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander. Mountbatten came later in 1947 as Viceroy.

q: The 'Royal Indian Navy (RIN) Mutiny' of February 1946 began aboard which naval ship in Bombay?
exp: The RIN Ratings Revolt began on 18 February 1946 on HMIS Talwar in Bombay over racial discrimination and poor food conditions.
